rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and appropriately notes visible blastocoel, ICM, and TE, but it hedges on stage and introduces uncertainty versus the provided Gardner 3AA/expanded description; some image-specific details are inferred rather than clearly verifiable.

Integrates most relevant factors well, including age, prior IVF history, BMI, endometrium, semen parameters, diagnosis, and day-5 quality, though AMH is unavailable and some interactions are discussed somewhat generically.

Reasoning is logical and mostly internally consistent, with prognosis tied to embryo quality and patient age; minor issues include slight confusion around implantation versus clinical pregnancy/live birth framing and stage terminology.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice guidelines, especially support for single embryo transfer in a 30-year-old with a good-quality blastocyst and caution about overusing add-ons; minor imprecision around Gardner staging prevents a top score.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, luteal support adherence, activity guidance, and future evaluation after failure, but remains somewhat general rather than highly case-specific in contingency planning.
